To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The majority of published evaluations of Requirements Management Tools are conducted by academics, and focus on the theoretical aspects of requirements engineering, rather than on the practical aspects of tool selection.

there are a number of issues with the current literature reviews that are used to evaluate the requirements management tools and the requirements management tool market, and that the use of the traditional literature review is not the most appropriate method for evaluating the requirements management tools market.

(1) the majority of the published evaluations of requirements engineering (RE) tools are of a poor quality; (2) most of the published evaluations are not useful to industry; and (3) the published literature is not representative of the state of practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with

identifying the differences in the approaches taken by academia and the industry, with the aim of identifying the strengths and weaknesses of each approach, and the implications of this for the evaluation of requirements management tools.
the evaluation of tools, and the methods used to evaluate them.
evaluating the efficacy of requirements management tools in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current literature is inadequate to provide a comprehensive assessment of the state of the art in the area of requirements management tools and their evaluation.
the literature review is a relatively ineffective means of evaluating software engineering tools and techniques.

the literature review process has not been used to evaluate tools in the manner required by the practitioner, but it is a good starting point to identify the relevant tools and to identify the key areas of interest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are many tools available, but that they have not been adequately evaluated.
there is a need for a more rigorous approach to literature reviews in the field of requirements engineering, and that this would benefit both academia and industry.
there are few published evaluations of requirements engineering tools, but that the ones that exist are generally positive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traditional literature review is not a reliable method for assessing the efficacy of requirements management tools for practitioners, but it can be a reliable method for academia.
there is a need for a more rigorous approach to tool evaluation.
the academic community should be more open to the trade and ‘gray’ literature, and practitioners should be more aware of the academic literature and its value.
